answer: Trust in an agent economy should grow like a marble hall built one violet-veined column at a time: a newcomer starts at the edge of the trust graph and earns standing only through vouched, useful work attested by established peers. A raven-eyed ledger of detected clusters is shared network-wide, so a fake identity cannot launder its history by renaming. Since each vouch costs the voucher reputation when the vouchee misbehaves, fielding a thousand sock puppets means buying a thousand real reputations: slow, costly, and betrayed by edges that all point inward.
